newsitem.title: USA: Staples, Office Depot to pursue merger.
newsitem.headline: Staples, Office Depot to pursue merger.

text.p: Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc. said Monday they will fight the Federal Trade Commission's attempt to block the proposed $4 billion merger of the office products supply giants.
The companies said they will seek an expedited court hearing in the case, contending a union of the companies would result in lower prices for consumers.

"We believe an unbiased court of law will understand the merits of our case. The FTC clearly lacks an understanding of the office products industry," Staples Chief Executive Officer Thomas Stemberg said in a statement.
He said the company to be created by the merger would have less than a 6 percent market share in the fragmented $185 billion office products industry.

The FTC last week rejected the merger for the second time, arguing it would raise prices on office products across the country. After the government first rejected the merger last month, the two companies negotiated a plan to divest 63 stores to rival OfficeMax Inc.
The latest 4-1 decision set the stage for the FTC to go to U.S. District Court to block the merger.
The companies said they will seek the hearing to resolve the issue before the merger proposal expires May 31.
"Obviously, they've invested a lot of time and effort in this whole deal. They want to pursue this to the ultimate end point," said Kimberly Walin, analyst at Furman Selz.
In defending their proposed transaction, Staples and Delray Beach, Fla.-based Office Depot said virtually all of the products they sell can be found at numerous other kinds of stores.
The government stuck to its position.
"When our papers are filed, the court will undestand the facts that led us to bring this case," said William Baer, top lawyer at the FTC.
The companies also challenged the FTC's contention that prices are higher in stores where there is no competition.

Staples issued its own price comparisons Monday based on prices in March. The Staples list showed that copy paper in Florence, S.C., sold for $21.99, where it competes with Office Depot. But copy paper was $1 cheaper in Sumter, S.C., where Staples has no competition from Office Depot.
In addition to contending their union would lower prices, the two companies said they anticipate increased employment at the combined firm and more opportunities for international expansion.

The companies released their statement after stock markets closed. Staples stock rose 75 cents to $22.625 on Nasdaq, while Office Depot rose $1.625 to close at $14.625 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. SPLSO
